tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.0.question: What is ASCII art?
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.0.answer: ASCII art uses the density of different characters to mimic the brightness of an image — denser characters represent darker areas and sparser characters represent brighter ones.
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.1.question: What does the width setting do?
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.1.answer: The width (number of columns) determines how many characters the output uses. More columns mean more detail but a wider result; fewer columns produce a more abstract look.
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.2.question: What does invert mean?
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.2.answer: Invert flips the brightness mapping, using sparse characters for dark areas and dense characters for bright ones — useful for displaying on dark backgrounds.
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.3.question: Can I save the result?
tools.image-to-ascii.faqs.3.answer: Yes. You can copy it to your clipboard with one click, or download it as a .txt file.

tools.css-sprite-generator.description: Combine multiple images into a single sprite sheet and automatically generate the matching CSS background-position code. Supports horizontal, vertical, and grid layouts.
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.0.answer: A sprite combines several small images into one larger image. CSS background-position is used to show just one part of it, reducing HTTP requests and speeding up loading.
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.1.questi: What's the difference between the three layouts?
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.1.answer: The horizontal layout arranges all images side by side, the vertical layout stacks them vertically, and the grid layout arranges them into rows and columns of roughly square cells.
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.2.questi: How do I use the generated CSS?
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.2.answer: Each icon corresponds to a .icon-N style containing its width, height, background image path, and negative offsets. Just copy it into your stylesheet.
tools.css-sprite-generator.faqs.3.questi: How many images can I combine at once?

tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.0.question: What's the difference between Blob URL and DataURL?
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.0.answer: A Blob URL (starting with blob:) points to an object in the browser's memory and is great for in-page use. A DataURL is a Base64-encoded string that can be embedded directly into HTML/CSS, making it easy to share and store.
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.1.question: Can a Blob URL be used long term?
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.1.answer: No. A Blob URL is only valid within the current page session and becomes invalid after a refresh or when the page is closed.
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.2.question: Are there any downsides to DataURL?
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.2.answer: Base64 encoding increases the size by about 33% and is not ideal for large images, but it's convenient for embedding directly in code.
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded to a server?
tools.blob-dataurl.faqs.3.answer: No. The conversion happens entirely locally in your browser.

tools.image-similarity.metadata.descript: Free online tool to calculate the similarity percentage, MSE, and PSNR of two images.
tools.image-similarity.title: Image Similarity
tools.image-similarity.description: Upload two images to calculate pixel-level similarity, mean squared error (MSE), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), with an adjustable tolerance threshold.
tools.image-similarity.faqs.0.question: How is similarity calculated?
tools.image-similarity.faqs.0.answer: The RGB values are compared pixel by pixel. Two pixels are considered similar when their color difference is within the tolerance, and the similarity percentage is the proportion of similar pixels.
tools.image-similarity.faqs.1.question: What do MSE and PSNR mean?
tools.image-similarity.faqs.1.answer: MSE (mean squared error) is smaller when the two images are closer. PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio) is measured in dB — above 30 dB generally indicates near-lossless quality.
tools.image-similarity.faqs.2.question: What happens if I increase the tolerance?
tools.image-similarity.faqs.2.answer: A larger tolerance treats pixels with small color differences as similar, so similarity increases. A smaller tolerance makes the comparison stricter.
tools.image-similarity.faqs.3.question: Can images of different sizes be compared?
tools.image-similarity.faqs.3.answer: Yes. The tool scales both images to the same size before comparing them pixel by pixel.

tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.0.quest: How do I set the frame extraction interval?
tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.0.answe: The interval is how often a frame is captured, in seconds. A smaller interval gives more, smoother frames; a larger interval gives fewer frames and saves storage space.
tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.1.quest: What is the maximum number of frames I can extract?
tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.1.answe: To protect browser memory, up to 100 frames can be extracted at a time. We recommend increasing the interval or trimming the video first.
tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.2.quest: What formats can I save to?

tools.video-frame-extractor.faqs.3.quest: Is my video uploaded to a server?

tools.animated-webp.faqs.0.question: What is the difference between animated WebP and GIF?
tools.animated-webp.faqs.0.answer: At the same visual quality, an animated WebP is usually only 30%-50% of a GIF's size, supports 16 million colors, and compresses better — though some older platforms don't support it.
tools.animated-webp.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between lossless and lossy?
tools.animated-webp.faqs.1.answer: Lossless compression keeps full quality but produces larger files; lossy compression slightly reduces quality for much smaller files, which suits photo-like content.
tools.animated-webp.faqs.2.question: Will the generated WebP loop automatically?
tools.animated-webp.faqs.2.answer: Yes. The converted animated WebP loops infinitely by default.
tools.animated-webp.faqs.3.question: How long does the conversion take?
tools.animated-webp.faqs.3.answer: The first run downloads the ~30MB FFmpeg engine (cached afterwards); then conversion speed depends on the video's length and resolution.
